Figure 3:GeoSET framework.Stage 1 initializes a SAR encoder from a
pretrained autoencoder and trains it to reconstruct the original SAR
observation from a domain-aware speckle perturbation while the shared decoder
remains frozen. Stage 2 replaces the pretrained generator’s text condition
with a spatial SAR stream initialized from its image stream and learns a
conditional flow from Gaussian noise to the EO latent. Stage 3 adapts the
resulting generalist to each downstream benchmark with LoRA or full fine-tuning.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison on SAR-to-EO image translation (SET) benchmarks.All methods receive the same SAR observation, and the paired EO image
is shown as a reference.
Figure 6:Qualitative comparison on the QXS-SAROPT dataset.All methods receive identical SAR inputs, with paired EO images shown as references.
Figure 7:Qualitative comparison on the SAR2Opt dataset.All methods receive identical SAR inputs, with paired EO images shown as references.
Figure 8:Qualitative comparison on the SAR2EO dataset.All methods receive identical SAR inputs, with paired EO images shown as references.
Figure 9:Qualitative comparison on the SpaceNet6 dataset.All methods receive identical SAR inputs, with paired EO images shown as references.

Figure 10:SAR and EO reconstruction across pretraining sources.Top: reconstructions of original SAR and EO inputs.
Bottom: speckle-perturbed SAR inputs (L=4L=4, left) and their reconstructions (right).
Values indicate PSNR (dB) relative to the corresponding original
observations; parenthesized values refer to perturbed inputs.

Figure 11:Domain-aware speckle augmentation across pretraining sources.From left to right: original SAR inputs and perturbed inputs withL=16L=16,88, and44. SmallerLLyields stronger perturbations.
Values indicate PSNR (dB) relative to the original SAR observations.
